newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BACK IN THE OLD ROUTINE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BACK IN THE OLD ROUTINE.

text.p: Defending champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov took another confident step towards the retention of his French Open crown on Wednesday, marching into the third round with his second consecutive straight sets victory.

The Russian third seed beat France's Guillaume Raoux 7-5 6-3 6-4 in one hour 34 minutes and believes he may be on the brink of rediscovering his best form at precisely the right time following a lengthy injury absence.

"I am very satisfied with my first two rounds," said Kafelnikov, who now faces another French opponent in the shape of Cedric Pioline. "Winning twice in straight sets has also allowed to me to save energy before my match with Cedric."

The world number three was out of action for three months with a broken finger sustained while using a punch-bag before the Australian Open in January, yet has already surpassed most expectations at Roland Garros.

En route to the title a year ago he only dropped one set in the entire fortnight, against Dutchman Richard Krajicek in the quarter-finals, but his more recent first round defeats in both Barcelona and Monte Carlo last month now appear mere temporary blips.
On another dry, sunny day, there was little else among the early matches to rouse the Parisian crowds.

Spain's Alex Corretja was a 4-6 6-1 6-1 7-6 winner against Germany's Jens Knippschild despite feeling less than 100 percent beforehand, while women's fourth seed Jana Novotna also overcame a poor start against German opponent Jana Kandarr.

The willowy Kandarr, wearing what fashion connoisseurs at Roland Garros suggested was the shortest skirt of the tournament to date, led 4-1 in the first set only for Novotna to reel off 11 successive games to win 6-4 6-0.

The veteran Czech knows she needs to produce more of the same if she is to stand a chance of winning the title and, her confidence boosted by a new racket, has already decided on a more attacking strategy.
"I have to be more aggressive at important moments and not try to wait for my opponents' mistakes," she said. "I've just got to go out there and win it myself."
Seventh seed Conchita Martinez cruised past the flimsy challenge of American Chanda Rubin to win 6-3 6-0 and stay on course for a quarter-final meeting with Steffi Graf.
